bull.b: Rapid growth in HPC leasing is shifting TeraWulf toward contracted infrastructure revenue rather than relying solely on bitcoin mining. Rising lease contribution and Lake Mariner’s operating capacity provide a more durable commercial foundation, supporting revenue visibility as additional halls come online.

The large, long-term Anthropic lease, Google credit support, and Fluor construction framework materially strengthen the Justified project’s bankability and execution structure. If milestones are delivered, these commitments could convert strong AI infrastructure demand into substantial recurring revenue over multiple years.

A substantial liquidity position gives TeraWulf resources to fund contracted Lake Mariner and Justified commitments while Muskie expands its long-term capacity opportunity. Access to a potential gigawatt of power also supports scalable HPC development in an environment management describes as power constrained.

bear.b: The current revenue base is not yet sufficient to absorb operating and other expenses, leaving TeraWulf deeply loss-making below gross profit. Persistent negative earnings weaken internal funding capacity, increase dependence on financing, and make successful project ramp-up essential to improving the business model.

Large recurring cash outflows indicate that expansion is consuming substantial funding before the platform reaches self-financing scale. Negative operating and free cash flow can constrain flexibility, increase reliance on debt or other capital sources, and leave less room to absorb project delays or cost escalation.

Significant remaining committed construction spending creates ongoing execution and financing exposure even with contracted demand. Capital must be deployed successfully before the related capacity can generate its intended revenue, while higher financing costs and infrastructure funding needs could pressure returns and financial flexibility.
